answer: The ledger locks 500 credits per agent key. When a fraud proof lands, say on a rigged garden-irrigation plan flagged at dawn, each convicted key loses k² percent, where k is the public count of keys caught in that 100-block window. One cheat loses 5 credits, five lose 125 each, and ten lose all, so every added fake deepens a spiral of loss. Fakes must strike together to sway outcomes, and each needs its own deposit, so they can't be spread out or shared.
